source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension (នាយកដ្ឋានផ្សព្វផ្សាយកសិកម្ម) - "ដំណាំក្រូចពោធិសាត់" (Pursat Orange Cultivation Guide), 2016, 26pp
text:
Pruning (បច្ចេកទេសកាត់តម្រូវឲ្យមានផលទាន់ពេលវេលា) is used to keep the tree's canopy open and to encourage new flowering wood so that fruiting happens on a predictable schedule. Farmers should remove crowded, crossing, or diseased branches, and cut back old unproductive wood to stimulate fresh growth.

Any shoots (suckers) that emerge from below the graft union should be removed promptly, since they come from the rootstock variety and will not produce the desired Pursat orange fruit if left to grow. Pruning is best carried out before the main flowering period so the tree channels its energy into the new growth that will carry the coming crop.
